neighbours.label: 'take/taken' in the idiom 'take ... for granted' (a predictor of 'for granted'), as opposed to 'take' in its other senses (take the train, take a walk, take donations)
fire: Electricity is something most households take for granted until a storm hits.
Kind teachers are too often taken for granted by busy parents.
We should never take our freedoms for granted.
Reliable internet is now taken for granted in most offices.
Small acts of kindness are easily taken for granted.
Many workers take paid holidays for granted these days.
Children often take their parents' patience for granted.
Public libraries are a service that many towns take for granted.
quiet: Electricity bills take a large share of most household budgets.
Kind teachers often take extra time to help struggling students.
We should take a walk after dinner tonight.
Reliable internet takes years to build in rural areas.
Small acts of kindness take very little effort.
Many workers take the train to the office every morning.
Children often take their parents' old toys to the park.
Public libraries take donations of used books every Saturday.
